description:
Why this choice is correct: crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:30 carries 'Workspace tracking: bd:JMAP-sc1b.105.' inline in the file-level doc comment. The bench file is thus self-describing — a future reader who finds it without context can run 'bd show JMAP-sc1b.105' and recover the original requirements (workload sizes, acceptance criteria, design rationale) immediately.

This matches the workspace pattern established in crate-jmap-base-client/benches/session_and_urls.rs (cites JMAP-sc1b.106) and crate-jmap-server/benches/dispatcher.rs. Keep the citation idiom for any future bench file.

A future contributor might suggest 'cleaning up' the citation as a TODO-like comment that should not survive the bead's closure. Reject that suggestion. The bead-citation is permanent provenance, not a TODO. It links the artifact to its design discussion forever, even after the bead closes (which it has — JMAP-sc1b.105 is CLOSED).

Same applies to examples/parse_eml.rs: tracking bd:JMAP-sc1b.17.1 should remain in the commit message and any future docstring that gets added (currently the example does not cite its bead inline; that is a small readability gap but not worth a finding by itself).
title: Bench file cites bd:JMAP-sc1b.105 inline; workspace tracking explicit
